articles.title: Flávio Bolsonaro promete combate às queimadas em Manaus, caso eleito | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato do PL à Presidência da República participou de evento aberto ao público durante agenda em Manaus, na noite de segunda-feira (19).
articles.summary: Em agenda em Manaus, Flávio Bolsonaro prometeu intensificar o combate às queimadas na Amazônia e investir em infraestrutura caso vença as eleições presidenciais.
articles.body:
Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) durante evento com apoiadores em Manaus na noite de segunda-feira (19). — Foto: Patrick Marques/g1 AM

O candidato do PL à Presidência da República, Flávio Bolsonaro , prometeu ajudar o Amazonas no combate às queimadas florestais caso seja eleito. A promessa foi feita durante um evento aberto ao público em Manaus , na noite desta segunda-feira (19).

"A partir de janeiro do ano que vem, vocês terão um presidente que vai ajudar o estado do Amazonas a combater as queimadas", disse Flávio, sem detalhar medidas.

Acompanhado por apoiadores e pela candidata ao governo do Amazonas, Professora Maria do Carmo (PL), ele também criticou a atuação de Lula frente ao problema ambiental que atinge diferentes municípios no estado e fez com que Manaus ficasse mais de dez dias encoberta por fumaça .

O Lula tá cagando pra Amazônia. A partir do ano que vem vocês terão um presidente que protege a floresta."

Ainda em discurso, Flávio Bolsonaro também prometeu melhorias na infraestrutura do estado. Ele citou a rodovia BR-319, que passa por entraves quanto a liberação da licença ambiental para asfaltamento, e a Zona Franca de Manaus.

"O presidente Flávio Bolsonaro vai estar atento para infraestrutura do Amazonas. A BR-319 vai sair. A Zona Franca de Manaus vai gerar emprego e oportunidade pra cada um de vocês."

O ato político foi o único compromisso de Flávio na capital amazonense. Ele chegou a Manaus pela tarde, após cumprir agenda em Marabá, no Pará.

Uma série de incêndios foram registrados na Região Metropolitana de Manaus e em municípios do interior do Amazonas desde o fim de agosto. O avanço das chamas fez com que a capital e municípios como Itacoatiara, Manacapuru e Autazes, ficassem encobertos por fumaça.

Na capital, a rotina da cidade foi afetada com o cancelamento de atividades ao ar livre e de aulas da rede pública de ensino. A Universidade Federal do Amazonas (Ufam) e a Universidade do Estado do Amazonas (UEA) também suspenderam as atividades .

O governo federal anunciou, no domingo (18), o reforço das operações de combate às queimadas no Amazonas , com aumento para 16 aeronaves, mobilização de quatro esquadrões de helicópteros, dois navios e mais brigadistas.

As medidas incluem a criação de um Estado-Maior Conjunto para coordenar a atuação das Forças Armadas e dos órgãos envolvidos no combate aos incêndios florestais, que avançam no estado e provocam fumaça em Manaus.

Na área da saúde, uma base descentralizada da Força Nacional do SUS será instalada em Manaus na terça-feira (20). A estrutura deve ampliar a capacidade de resposta diante de possíveis impactos da fumaça sobre a saúde dos moradores.

articles.title: Receita Federal notifica quase meio milhão de contribuintes que caíram na malha fina | G1
articles.standfirst: Na grande maioria dos casos, erros simples levaram contribuintes à malha fina. Mas, para resolver o problema, não é preciso buscar um posto da Receita Federal. Basta ter acesso a um computador ou ao celular.
articles.summary: Na grande maioria dos casos, erros simples levaram contribuintes à malha fina. Mas, para resolver o problema, não é preciso buscar um posto da Receita Federal. Basta ter acesso a um computador ou ao celular.
articles.body:
Parte dos brasileiros que caíram na malha fina vai receber uma carta da Receita Federal em outubro. É um aviso de que esses contribuintes cometeram pequenos erros e ainda podem regularizar, pela internet, a declaração do Imposto de Renda.

A Receita Federal tem quase 6 milhões de contribuintes caíram na malha fina. O funcionário público Alexsandre de Sá Gomes é um deles. Sempre fez a declaração sozinho, mas dessa vez cometeu uma falha que vai precisar corrigir para receber a restituição.

“Foi um erro de interpretação meu. Eu interpretei um dado de forma equivocada e isso me gerou essa consequência. Eu poderia estar recebendo algo e agora tenho que aguardar”, conta.

não informar algum rendimento extra, pontual, que recebeu durante o ano;

não incluir rendimentos recebidos por dependentes;

informar o ano errado de uma despesa médica;

não informar todos os rendimentos da aposentadoria, quando há mais de uma fonte pagadora.

Na grande maioria dos casos, erros simples levaram contribuintes à malha fina. Mas, para resolver o problema, não é preciso buscar um posto da Receita Federal. Basta ter acesso a um computador ou a um telefone celular. Para saber se você caiu na malha fina, é só entrar no portal e-CAC ou usar o aplicativo da Receita Federal, disponível para celular ou tablet. Faça o login pela conta gov.br - é obrigatório que você seja usuário prata ou ouro, que são níveis mais altos de segurança, para verificar a identidade. Clique na opção “Meu Imposto de Renda” e preste atenção ao status. Se aparecer “com pendências”, clique para saber o problema encontrado pela Receita e faça a retificação.

Receita Federal notifica quase meio milhão de contribuintes que caíram na malha fina — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

Para acelerar o processo, a Receita enviou cartas para quase meio milhão de contribuintes para que eles façam as retificações online.

“São aqueles casos mais simples em que ele próprio pode se autorregularizar. Os outros casos são mais complexos, não tem como se autorregularizar. Ele tem que demostrar com documentações, abrindo processos. Tudo de forma digital”, afirma Jorge Alberto dos Santos, auditor fiscal da Receita Federal.

Em qualquer caso, quem entende do assunto recomenda rapidez.

“Essa divergência pode ser encaminhada, ser direcionada a um lançamento fiscal e, caso seja feito esse lançamento fiscal, ele pode virar uma dívida ativa, uma cobrança, e essa dívida do contribuinte pode, inclusive, dobrar”, explica Edilson Junior, vice-presidente do Conselho Regional de Contabilidade do RJ.

“Retificando, ela é automaticamente reprocessada e ele, tendo direito, o contribuinte tendo direito à restituição, ele vai entrar na fila de restituição”, diz Jorge Alberto dos Santos, auditor fiscal da Receita Federal.

articles.title: Mesmo quem não votou no primeiro turno pode votar no segundo | G1
articles.standfirst: No dia 4 de outubro, mais de 33,4 milhões de eleitores, 21% dos brasileiros aptos, não votaram.
articles.summary: No dia 4 de outubro, mais de 33,4 milhões de eleitores, 21% dos brasileiros aptos, não votaram.
articles.body:
Quem não votou no primeiro turno está apto a votar no segundo turno.

Mesmo de plantão em UTIs, a médica Rosana Nakamura sempre deu um jeito de votar, contando com a colaboração de colegas e eleitores.

“Eu explicava: ‘Ó, estou de plantão, vim aqui exclusivamente só para votar e eu preciso voltar para o plantão’. Então, todo mundo sempre colaborou em relação a isso”, diz.

Dessa vez tentou, mas não conseguiu trocar a passagem de uma viagem ao exterior, usou a tecnologia do GPS no e-Título para justificar a ausência.

“A gente entrou no aplicativo, ele já detectou que a gente estava fora do Brasil”, conta Rosana Nakamura.

Mas, no segundo turno, ela estará presente para votar:

“Sim, é um direito que a gente conquistou com muito esforço. Então, a gente tem que fazer a nossa parte como cidadão”.

Mesmo quem não votou no primeiro pode votar no segundo turno — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

Usar o e-Título ou ida ao cartório eleitoral para justificar a ausência é uma necessidade. O prazo para o primeiro turno é até 3 de dezembro. Isso evita multas, cancelamento do título a partir de três ausências e punições - como impedimento para tirar passaporte, receber salário no serviço público ou se inscrever em universidades públicas.

No primeiro turno, mais de 33,4 milhões de eleitores, 21% dos brasileiros aptos, não compareceram. Mas isso não impede o voto no segundo turno das eleições. Uma participação que fortalece a cidadania e a democracia.

“A Justiça Eleitoral vem colocando medidas para ampliar a participação. A gente só tem democracia se a gente tiver uma ampla participação de todos no processo eleitoral”, afirma Luna Chino, coordenadora de gestão de eleições do TRE-SP.

A rapidez da votação no segundo turno pode facilitar a vida do eleitor.

“Principalmente porque agora no segundo turno, em grande parte dos estados, as pessoas vão votar no máximo em dois cargos. É uma votação mais rápida, uma votação mais ágil”, diz Luna Chino.

articles.title: Despedida a Benito Di Paula será no Theatro Municipal de São Paulo, em cerimônia aberta ao público | G1
articles.standfirst: Cantor e compositor tratava um câncer de próstata e morreu no domingo (18), aos 84 anos.
articles.summary: Cantor e compositor tratava um câncer de próstata e morreu no domingo (18), aos 84 anos.
articles.body:
A despedida ao cantor e compositor Benito Di Paula vai ser nesta terça-feira (20) no Theatro Municipal de São Paulo, em uma cerimônia aberta ao público. Ele morreu neste domingo (18) aos 84 anos.

O Brasil fez o samba, e o samba de Benito Di Paula. Letra romântica, melodia fácil de cantar, arranjos e acessórios exuberantes.

“As pessoas implicavam muito com o visual dele. O Benito se dizia descendente de ciganos, então tinha aquele anel de ouro, aquele cabelo, os ternos”, conta o jornalista e crítico musical Sérgio Martins.

Na certidão de nascimento, era Uday Vellozo. Nasceu em Nova Friburgo, na Serra Fluminense. Cresceu em uma família de pouco dinheiro, em uma casa cheia de música. O pai ensinou os primeiros acordes no violão. O piano, ele aprendeu depois por conta própria. E foi se apresentando na noite, em boates do Rio, Santos e São Paulo que ele encontrou um jeito próprio de tocar o público. Sentava ao piano como se fosse começar uma conversa. Como se tivesse uma história bonita para contar. "Retalhos de Cetim" foi o primeiro grande sucesso em 1973.

“Fiz ‘Retalhos de Cetim’ porque eu imaginei a luta que é para colocar uma escola de samba na rua, é uma dificuldade, é um trabalho de arte geral”, contou Benito Di Paula no programa "Conversa com Bial" que foi ao ar em 11 de novembro de 2022.

Despedida a Benito Di Paula será no Theatro Municipal de São Paulo, em cerimônia aberta ao público — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

Dos quadrinhos que lia em uma pensão de italianos, veio a ideia de apresentar o Brasil para um amigo estrangeiro. Um sucesso atrás do outro.

“Benito foi um cara muito corajoso, muito inventivo, em um tempo de muito purismo ainda na música brasileira”, diz o cantor Zeca Baleiro.

O filho herdou a voz afinada e o talento para o piano. Foi com Rodrigo Vellozo o último show. A música de Benito Di Paula fica como legado para muitas gerações de artistas. Outras rodas de samba, pequenas e grandes. Em 2025, uma homenagem do carnaval paulistano emocionou o artista. O cantor e compositor Xande de Pilares, o fã que virou amigo, estava lá:

“Seu legado fica aqui para a gente e para quem quiser usufruir da sua obra. Descanse em paz, meu amigo”.

Benito tratava um câncer de próstata e morreu na noite de domingo (18), aos 84 anos. Mas a música dele não vai parar de tocar.

articles.title: Presidente Lula, candidato à reeleição pelo PT, faz campanha no Rio Grande do Sul | G1
articles.standfirst: Em Porto Alegre, candidato destacou o pacote de medidas para microempreendedores individuais.
articles.summary: Em Porto Alegre, candidato destacou o pacote de medidas para microempreendedores individuais.
articles.body:
O presidente Lula , candidato à reeleição pelo PT , cumpriu agenda no Rio Grande do Sul.

A agenda de campanha do candidato do PT foi em Porto Alegre. Ele chegou à cidade no meio da tarde. A concentração dos apoiadores para receber Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva começou por volta das 16h no Largo dos Açorianos, uma praça histórica localizada no Centro da capital gaúcha.

Lula destacou o pacote de medidas para microempreendedores individuais:

“O Estado brasileiro anistiou uma dívida de R$ 15 bilhões dos MEIs que estavam devendo. Era uma dívida ativa que estava na conta da União, dívida que as pessoas não iam poder pagar. Então, a gente resolveu anistiar. Nós vamos comprar a dívida das pessoas que estão devendo, vamos fazer um leilão dessa dívida e vamos garantir... Nós esperamos comprar com desconto de uns 95% para que as pessoas fiquem livres de uma dívida impagável, que foi contraída desde o tempo da Covid. E, ao mesmo tempo, nós vamos anunciar uma outra coisa. Nós vamos liberar um PIX de R$ 5 mil para cada pessoa que se livrar da dívida, para que ele tenha um... Não é empréstimo. É o Estado garantindo que essas pessoas comecem uma nova vida sem ficar devendo”.

Em seguida, o candidato subiu em um carro de som e saiu em passeata cercado de eleitores. Ele percorreu cerca de dez quarteirões no Centro Histórico da capital gaúcha. Lula discursou para os apoiadores. O ato terminou ao lado do Mercado Público de Porto Alegre.

Sem a presença do candidato, apoiadores da reeleição de Lula estiveram nas ruas de Teresina, com um ato que começou em frente à Assembleia Legislativa e seguiu pelas principais ruas da cidade. E, em Fortaleza, uma manifestação foi no bairro Parangaba, na periferia da cidade.

articles.title: Flávio Bolsonaro, candidato do PL à Presidência, faz campanha no Amazonas e no Pará | G1
articles.standfirst: Em Marabá, candidato falou sobre combate à violência e fez críticas ao que chamou de entraves ambientais.
articles.summary: Em Marabá, candidato falou sobre combate à violência e fez críticas ao que chamou de entraves ambientais.
articles.body:
O Jornal Nacional mostrou como foi o dia dos candidatos à Presidência da República nesta segunda-feira (19). Flávio Bolsonaro , do PL , fez campanha no Amazonas e no Pará.

O primeiro compromisso do dia de Flávio Bolsonaro foi em Marabá, no sudoeste do Pará. O candidato foi recebido por eleitores no aeroporto. De lá, saiu em carreata pelas principais ruas da cidade. Flávio Bolsonaro estava acompanhado do governador eleito do Pará, Doutor Daniel, do Podemos.

Do alto de um trio elétrico, o candidato do PL discursou para apoiadores. Ele falou sobre combate à violência, fez críticas ao que chamou de entraves ambientais e disse que, se for eleito, vai investir na infraestrutura na região. A economia de Marabá tem forte influência de atividades como a mineração e a agropecuária:

“Porque eu quero me comprometer aqui, Daniel, com todas essas obras que são necessárias aqui em Marabá, como as duas pontes que precisam ser finalizadas, com as estradas federais que são necessárias ser asfaltadas aqui. Eu vou fazer a maior regularização fundiária que o Pará já viu e a sua terra vai passar para a sua pessoa no papel. Vamos respeitar a propriedade privada. Você vai poder plantar, criar gado, vai fazer o que quiser na sua terra, e o que você explorar da terra é seu. Esses entraves que existem, ambientais e principalmente por causa de razões ideológicas, a gente vai acabar. E eu vou, a partir de janeiro do ano que vem, declarar guerra aos narcoterroristas desse país. É assim que a gente vai levar esse país: fazendo com que a lei valha para todo mundo”.

Flávio Bolsonaro chegou a Manaus por volta das 14h e foi direto para um hotel, onde ficou até a hora do evento com eleitores no Complexo Turístico da Ponta Negra.

articles.title: Desvio no Ideflor-Bio: Ex-presidente e esposa são denunciados no PA | G1
articles.standfirst: Ministério Público do Pará denunciou um suposto desvio de mais de R$ 14 milhões em contratos do Ideflor-Bio. Investigação aponta suspeitas de fraudes em licitações e irregularidades em serviços.
articles.summary: MPPA denuncia ex-presidente do Ideflor-Bio e esposa por desvios de R$ 14 milhões. Investigação aponta fraudes em licitações e compra de artigos de luxo.
articles.body:
MP denuncia suposto desvio de mais de R$ 14 milhões em contratos do Ideflor-Bio, no Pará. — Foto: Reprodução

O Ministério Público do Estado do Pará (MPPA) denunciou à Justiça um suposto esquema que teria desviado mais de R$ 14 milhões em contratos do Instituto de Desenvolvimento Florestal e da Biodiversidade do Pará (Ideflor-Bio).

Entre os denunciados estão o ex-presidente do instituto, Nilson Pinto de Oliveira , e a mulher dele, Lena Ribeiro Pinto . Segundo o MP, há suspeitas de direcionamento de licitações e irregularidades na execução dos serviços.

As denúncias foram formalizadas na 10ª Vara Criminal de Belém e ainda dependem de análise judicial.

Em nota, Nilson Pinto afirmou, em nota, que recebeu a denúncia com indignação, mas disse estar tranquilo e confiante na Justiça.

Segundo ele, todos os ritos legais foram cumpridos nos processos de contratação das empresas responsáveis pelos serviços.

Lena Pinto, a vereadora de Bragança Tatiana Ferreira Rodrigues e o Ideflor-Bio não se pronunciaram sobre as acusações.

A investigação tem como foco três contratos firmados entre o Ideflor-Bio e a Construtora Duas Marias . Eles previam:

Manutenção do muro do Parque Estadual do Utinga;

A vereadora de Bragança Tatiana Ferreira Rodrigues também está entre os investigados. Ela é apontada pelo MP como gestora da empresa contratada.

A apuração começou em maio deste ano e analisa operações financeiras realizadas entre fevereiro de 2023 e março de 2026.

Segundo o Ministério Público, os indícios foram identificados a partir de documentos administrativos e fiscais, registros bancários e outras informações obtidas com autorização judicial.

Segundo o promotor de Justiça Lauro Freitas, a Promotoria de Defesa do Patrimônio Público recebeu uma denúncia de que os contratos não eram compatíveis com a condição financeira, o porte e a estrutura da construtora Duas Marias.

"A construtora apresentou um crescimento financeiro brusco em pouco tempo, apesar de não ter estrutura financeira para prestar os serviços ao instituto".

Além do suposto direcionamento de licitações, o MP aponta:

Possíveis irregularidades na execução dos serviços;

Movimentações financeiras entre a empresa contratada, intermediários e integrantes do grupo apontado como beneficiário.

De acordo com Lauro Freitas, a análise identificou repasses a terceiros após a entrada dos pagamentos na conta da construtora.

Segundo ele, "foram detectados retornos financeiros para o então presidente do instituto, servidores e a esposa de Nilson Pinto, sem que fosse possível identificar o retorno desses recursos em serviços ao Ideflor-Bio".

De acordo com a investigação, recursos públicos teriam sido usados para comprar imóveis no exterior e artigos de luxo.

Entre os crimes investigados estão associação criminosa, lavagem de capitais e corrupção ativa.

Outras pessoas também foram denunciadas por suposta participação nas irregularidades. Segundo o Ministério Público, o valor dos danos aos cofres públicos ainda pode ser atualizado ao longo do processo.

O MP solicitou o afastamento de Nilson Pinto da presidência do Ideflor-Bio e de Lena Pinto, que era servidora da Secretaria de Estado de Educação (Seduc) cedida ao instituto. O casal deixou os cargos em julho deste ano.

articles.title: Viral video: French husband forces wife to return clothes she stole during protests amid France looting
articles.summary: A street scene has sparked a debate about rules, honesty and personal responsibility.
articles.body: A street scene has sparked a debate about rules, honesty and personal responsibility. The world is already aware of what’s going on in many cities of France these days. But amid the ongoing protest and loot, a brief confrontation outside a clothing store has caught people’s attention for all the right reasons.As images of looting and vandalised shops circulated on social media, a video showed a man intervening when a woman, reportedly his wife, appeared to leave a shop with a large bundle of clothes. Rather than letting her walk away with the luxury clothing, he took them away from her and carried them back to the store.The footage shows the shop as a Pimkie outlet. The video soon began circulating on social media and has gone viral.What made it viralWhat made the incident stand out was not simply the act of returning the clothes amid all the loot. It was the contrast between the two people's actions at the same time. At a time when some people were busy taking advantage of the protest situation, the man stood up for what’s right. He went against his wife and took all the garments back inside the store which shows his righteousness.The woman in the video can be seen with a pushchair and children closeby. She can be seen with a substantial quantity of clothing. The man then looks at her and takes all the garments from her hands only to return them.It’s a brief sequence, but conveyed a clear message; what’s wrong is wrong. While the woman appeared to be leaving with the clothes, the man made an effort to put them back.France's unrest puts looting in the spotlightOn October 17, 2026, demonstrations escalated into violence and looting in several French cities, including Paris, Marseille, Lyon and Bordeaux, among others, according to the Financial Times. The video emerged against this backdrop and that’s why the man’s act means a lot.Another report by Le Monde, described the damage to shops around Paris's Place de la République and Boulevard Magenta. Shopkeepers reported missing merchandise, smashed windows and extensive damage.People’s reactionWitnesses describe instances where law enforcement constraints were bypassed by familial intervention to restore stolen property. articles.standfirst: Agronegócio, indústria, setor automotivo, saúde e tecnologia aparecem entre os segmentos aquecidos para 2027.
articles.summary: Profissões em alta em Porto Alegre nos setores de tecnologia, agronegócio e saúde terão salários de até R$ 80 mil em 2027, aponta o novo Guia Salarial Robert Half.
articles.body:
Vista de Porto Alegre — Foto: Bruno Alencastro/ Agencia RBS

Profissionais das áreas fiscal, contábil, financeira, de compras e suprimentos e de tecnologia devem estar entre os mais procurados no Rio Grande do Sul em 2027, segundo o novo Guia Salarial da Robert Half.

O levantamento aponta agronegócio, indústria e manufatura, siderurgia e metalurgia, setor automotivo, saúde e tecnologia como os segmentos mais aquecidos no estado. As áreas que devem liderar as contratações são Recursos Humanos, Compras e Suprimentos, Fiscal, Contábil, Financeiro e Tecnologia.

As referências salariais do recorte gaúcho são de Porto Alegre. Entre os cargos mais bem remunerados está o de Chief Data Officer (CDO) no mercado financeiro, com faixa salarial de R$ 50 mil a R$ 80 mil.

Na área de tecnologia, gerente de dados tem remuneração entre R$ 22,5 mil e R$ 37,55 mil. Para especialista ou cientista de dados, os valores vão de R$ 16,05 mil a R$ 26,85 mil.

Na indústria, diretor de engenharia de empresa grande tem faixa salarial de R$ 36,85 mil a R$ 59,3 mil. Já gerente de planta pode receber entre R$ 28,5 mil e R$ 45,95 mil.

A reforma tributária também deve movimentar as contratações. Segundo a consultoria, os projetos de adequação envolvem setores como Fiscal, Compras, Tecnologia da Informação, Financeiro, Contabilidade e Jurídico.

Em Porto Alegre, gerente de Tax Transformation em empresa grande tem remuneração entre R$ 28 mil e R$ 42 mil. A faixa de gerente de planejamento tributário vai de R$ 24 mil a R$ 36 mil.

Veja salários de tecnologia e cargos de liderança

Os salários listados são baseados na remuneração real de profissionais que a Robert Half conectou a empregadores no Brasil. Eles representam a compensação inicial, ou seja, o pagamento de alguém novo na empresa para o cargo indicado, sem bônus ou benefícios.

A primeira faixa corresponde ao candidato novo no cargo ou que ainda desenvolve habilidades relevantes. A última representa o profissional mais experiente, com especializações e certificações.

O valor intermediário não representa a média salarial de todos os profissionais naquele cargo. Ele indica a remuneração de um candidato considerado intermediário em experiência e qualificação.

Reforma tributária deve movimentar contratações

A reforma tributária também deve ampliar a procura por profissionais. Segundo a consultoria, os projetos de adequação envolvem as áreas Fiscal, Compras, Tecnologia da Informação, Financeiro, Contabilidade e Jurídico.

Veja salários de cargos ligados à reforma tributária

A consultoria também aponta demanda por profissionais para apoiar processos de transformação e substituir trabalhadores deslocados temporariamente de suas funções habituais.

"No Rio Grande do Sul, a força do agronegócio, da indústria e do setor automotivo se reflete em projetos de transformação, implementação de sistemas e adequação de processos. Na saúde, há demanda ligada ao ciclo de receita, especialmente faturamento hospitalar, enquanto Tecnologia avança em automação, dados e IA. Esse cenário também amplia a procura por profissionais capazes de atuar em projetos e absorver demandas específicas", comenta a especialista de recrutamento da Robert Half, Bruna Martins.

articles.title: Masoud Pezeshkian: Peace, Not Surrender
articles.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on sanctions, regional conflict, US-Israel tensions and his call for Muslim unity.
articles.body:
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on sanctions, regional conflict, US-Israel tensions and his call for Muslim unity.

An exclusive Al Jazeera interview with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, by Al Jazeera Arabic’s Ali al-Dafiri at the United Nations in New York. Peace negotiations between the United States and Iran are struggling to make progress – but here Pezeshkian portrays Iran as the target of what he calls “terrorism”, pointing to the assassination of Iranian officials, scientists and schoolchildren in US and Israeli attacks. He addresses the serious impact of increased US sanctions on the Iranian economy, tensions around the Strait of Hormuz, and a series of broken agreements that, he argues, have destroyed Tehran’s trust in Washington. The president justifies Iran’s retaliatory strikes on US bases in the Gulf and the wider Arab region, arguing that regional security should be managed by local actors rather than foreign powers. He reflects on the wars in Gaza and Yemen, the new Syrian government, and Iran’s relationships with Russia and China – while calling for Muslim solidarity, anchored by Saudi Arabia, to counter what he sees as US-Israeli attempts to divide the region.

articles.summary: As operações de busca e resgate foram concluídas, afirmou o governador de Nariño. Sete pessoas ficaram feridas.
articles.body:
Quatorze pessoas morreram e outras sete ficaram feridas após o desabamento de uma mina de ouro ilegal no sudoeste da Colômbia , informaram autoridades locais nesta segunda-feira (19).

O acidente ocorreu no setor rural de Chambero, no município de Santa Barbara de Iscuande, localizado na província de Nariño.

As operações de busca e resgate foram concluídas, afirmou o governador de Nariño, Luis Alfonso Escobar.

O governador apelou ao governo nacional, à Agência Nacional de Mineração e ao Ministério de Minas e Energia para que acelerem o processo de formalização dos garimpeiros ilegais e de pequena escala, a fim de melhorar as condições de trabalho e os padrões de segurança.

Em agosto, 13 pessoas morreram em um acidente de mineração semelhante na cidade de Policarpa, também em Nariño.

A mineração informal e não regulamentada é comum em áreas rurais da Colômbia , onde as operações frequentemente carecem de infraestrutura de segurança adequada, resultando em frequentes acidentes fatais.

articles.title: Empresa condenada a pagar R$ 800 mil por dano moral coletivo na Bahia | G1
articles.standfirst: Acidente de trabalho aconteceu em fábrica de Itabuna, no sul da Bahia, em 2024. Funcionário morreu após ser atingido por máquina.
articles.summary: Acidente de trabalho aconteceu em fábrica de Itabuna, no sul da Bahia, em 2024. Funcionário morreu após ser atingido por máquina.
articles.body:
Funcionário de fábrica morreu após sofrer acidente de trabalho em Itabuna — Foto: Reprodução/TV Santa Cruz

A empresa suíça Barry Callebaut foi condenada a pagar R$ 800 mil por danos morais coletivos, após um funcionário morrer na fábrica que a empresa mantém em Itabuna , no sul da Bahia. O acidente de trabalho ocorreu em 2024, mas a decisão foi divulgada pelo Ministério Público do Trabalho (MPT-BA) nesta terça-feira (20).

O g1 tenta contato com a empresa fabricante de chocolate. Ainda cabe recurso da decisão.

Na ocasião, o eletromecânico Jobson Almeida Bispo fazia a manutenção no motor de um equipamento, quando a roda passou sobre a tampa de uma caixa de passagem. A estrutura não suportou a carga, o equipamento tombou e Jobson foi atingido na cabeça.

O funcionário foi socorrido pelo Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu) e levado para um hospital, onde passou por cirurgia, mas não resistiu.

Segundo o MPT-BA, a empresa alegou que o acidente ocorreu por culpa exclusiva do trabalhador , que teria executado uma atividade diferente daquela para a qual havia sido designado, sem a autorização necessária.

Porém, nas investigações foram comprovadas falhas na identificação, no controle e na fiscalização dos riscos ocupacionais, além de condições inadequadas no local onde o serviço foi realizado.

A investigação também identificou problemas em outras estruturas do estabelecimento . Ficou provado que apenas 76% das tampas das caixas de passagem avaliadas estavam em boas condições, enquanto as outras tampas apresentavam vulnerabilidade à corrosão ou comprometimento estrutural, com indicação de substituição imediata.

Na sentença, o juiz considerou a gravidade das irregularidades, a morte do trabalhador, a capacidade econômica da empresa e as medidas corretivas adotadas após o acidente para estabelecer o valor da condenação

O valor de R$800 mil por dano moral coletivo será destinado ao Fundo de Promoção do Trabalho Decente (Funtrad). Segundo a decisão, os recursos poderão ser aplicados em iniciativas relacionadas à promoção do trabalho decente, à melhoria das condições laborais e à prevenção de acidentes de trabalho.

articles.title: Prazo, liquidez e perfil: entenda como escolher um investimento | G1
articles.standfirst: Gerente do Sicoob explica o que avaliar antes de aplicar recursos.
articles.summary: Gerente do Sicoob explica o que avaliar antes de aplicar recursos.
articles.body:
Saber onde investir parece uma decisão simples e fácil, quando a escolha é guiada pela maior rentabilidade da aplicação. Entretanto, antes de tomar essa decisão, é importante entender outros fatores, que podem fazer a diferença no resultado. Pensando nisso, especialista do Sicoob explica o que avaliar antes do investimento e como o prazo, liquidez, segurança e perfil podem ajudar na escolha.

Atuando no mercado financeiro há 29 anos, Tatiana da Conceição Neves Marques, gerente do Sicoob Campos Centro, destaca que a finalidade do recurso, o prazo para alcançar o objetivo e o momento em que o investidor vai precisar do dinheiro devem ser avaliados antes de escolher qualquer aplicação.

“A partir dessas respostas, fica mais fácil identificar as opções de investimento mais adequadas, afinal, cada objetivo exige um planejamento diferente. O dinheiro destinado a uma emergência, por exemplo, precisa estar disponível com facilidade. Já um recurso pensado para a aposentadoria, pode ter um horizonte de muitos anos”, pontuou.

Atuando no mercado financeiro há 29 anos, Tatiana da Conceição Neves Marques é gerente do Sicoob Campos Centro — Foto: Divulgação

Segundo a gerente, o prazo é um dos principais fatores na decisão e a liquidez mostra a facilidade de transformar o investimento novamente em dinheiro disponível.

“Se o investidor vai precisar do dinheiro em pouco tempo, é importante priorizar alternativas com maior previsibilidade e menor exposição a oscilações. É importante entender que não são todas as aplicações que permitem resgate imediato. Por isso, verificar se a liquidez do valor investido é compatível com a necessidade é essencial”, destacou.

O perfil do investidor ajuda a identificar a disposição e a capacidade de cada pessoa para lidar com riscos e oscilações. Nestes perfis, são encontrados o conservador, o moderado e o arrojado.

“Essa avaliação considera não apenas a expectativa de retorno, mas também como a pessoa se sente diante das variações dos investimentos. O conservador, por exemplo, prioriza a segurança. O moderado aceita algum risco em busca de melhores oportunidades de retorno. Já o arrojado, possui maior tolerância às oscilações”.

Para Tatiana, uma estratégia importante é a diversificação, através da busca de oportunidades dentro dos limites adequados ao perfil e aos objetivos de cada investidor. Distribuindo os recursos de maneira planejada entre diferentes alternativas, a escolha precisa ser consciente, considerando o investimento como um todo, lembrando que rentabilidade passada não é garantia de resultados futuros.

“Não existe um único investimento ideal para todas as pessoas. Cada investidor tem uma realidade financeira, objetivos, prazos e um perfil de risco diferente. Uma alternativa adequada para uma pessoa pode não fazer sentido para outra. Por isso, a escolha deve ser individualizada e estar alinhada ao planejamento financeiro de cada um”, concluiu a gerente.

Quando houver dúvidas, a busca pela orientação de um profissional pode ajudar o investidor a uma decisão mais assertiva. Para isso, o Sicoob ajuda tanto quem está começando a investir, quanto quem busca diversificar a carteira.

Com um portfólio diversificado de investimentos, a oferece alternativas como o Recibo de Depósito Cooperativo (RDC), que funciona de maneira similar ao CDB das instituições tradicionais; Letra de Crédito Imobiliário (LCI), renda fixa para financiar o setor imobiliário; Letra de Crédito do Agronegócio (LCA), que financia atividades do setor agropecuário; entre outras opções, atendendo a diferentes perfis, objetivos e prazos.

Um dos principais diferenciais do Sicoob é o modelo cooperativo. Quem se associa não é apenas cliente, mas dono do empreendimento, participando democraticamente das decisões e resultados financeiros, que são reinvestidos no desenvolvimento regional, promovendo um ciclo de prosperidade socioeconômica.

Agência Sicoob Campos Centro — Foto: Divulgação

Instituição financeira cooperativa, o Sicoob reúne mais de 10,2 milhões de cooperados e está presente em todos os estados brasileiros e no Distrito Federal. Oferece um portfólio completo de soluções financeiras, incluindo conta corrente, crédito, investimentos, cartões, previdência, consórcios, seguros, cobrança bancária e meios eletrônicos de pagamento. The alleged strategy now appears to be broader: high-profile shootings and threats aimed at projecting the Lawrence Bishnoi gang's reach, spreading fear and establishing its supremacy - with Bollywood celebrities, politicians and other influential people among those targeted.In the early 1990s, gangsters wielded considerable influence over the film industry, using threats, extortion and targeted killings to pressure producers, actors, financiers and distributors.Among those targeted were producers Mukesh Duggal and Javed Siddiqui, filmmaker Rajiv Rai, director Rakesh Roshan, Manmohan Shetty and music producer Gulshan Kumar. articles.title: Australian founder used her childhood sewing machine to create office-chair blankets; her business recorded $200,000 in sales in six months and targeted $1 million in 2026
articles.summary: A spilt coffee, a job loss and an unused childhood sewing machine helped inspire Jane Helman to create Warmür, an Australia-based business selling
articles.body: A spilt coffee, a job loss and an unused childhood sewing machine helped inspire Jane Helman to create Warmür, an Australia-based business selling blankets designed to drape over office chairs. The idea began as a solution to a practical problem: staying warm at a desk without looking as though she were wrapped in a conventional blanket during video calls. In an as-told-to account published by Entrepreneur in May 2026, Helman described how the business developed from a homemade prototype into a retail product. The publication’s editorial introduction reported approximately $200,000 in sales across direct sales and wholesale between July and December 2025, and cited a $1 million sales target for 2026. The target was a projection at the time of publication, not a confirmed result. That figure was a forecast at the time of publication, not a confirmed year-end result. Her account traces the idea from a homemade prototype to a business selling through online and retail channels.Warmür founder Jane Helman: a spilt coffee and a childhood sewing machineIn her as-told-to account for Entrepreneur, Helman said the idea began in February 2021, when she was living in Canada after being laid off. She recalled spending time at home reading while wrapped in a large, fuzzy blanket. One day, as she leaned forward to reach for a pen, the blanket knocked over her coffee. The incident made her reconsider how practical ordinary blankets were for someone working at a desk. She searched online for a wearable blanket that looked suitable for video calls, but the options she found were bulky or had designs that did not suit her taste. She wanted something that would drape neatly over an office chair while keeping her warm.Helman decided to make a prototype herself. She retrieved a sewing machine she had received at age 12 and began working on the idea, despite having little sewing experience. She experimented with fabrics and sought advice at a fabric store before developing a workable design. The first product attracted interest beyond her own needs. According to Helman's account, a friend’s brother asked her to make 10 blankets for employees at his insurance firm. That early request suggested that the product could appeal to other people who wanted to stay warm at work without relying on an ordinary blanket. Helman began selling the product through a website built using Shopify. At this stage, the business grew from a practical solution to a personal problem rather than from a fully developed retail strategy.How Warmür grew through Shopify, TikTok and Uncommon GoodsWarmür’s next stage came through a combination of online sales and retail interest. Helman began working at Shopify, where she gained experience with e-commerce while continuing to develop her own business. She initially relied on a local seamstress to make the blankets, selling them through her own website. Within the first year, a TikTok video featuring the product went viral. The attention brought the brand to the notice of Uncommon Goods, a retailer that wanted to stock the blankets. The opportunity also created a production challenge: the seamstress could not make the hundreds of units that a retail order might require.Helman began searching for a manufacturer that could handle larger orders. In her account for Entrepreneur, she said the search took 8 months. She eventually found a women-owned manufacturing facility in Toronto and worked with it for 3 years, until the business outgrew its production capacity. Helman described Warmür as entirely bootstrapped. She said pretty much all her savings went into the business and that she reinvested its earnings rather than seeking outside funding. She also described herself as the company’s only official employee, with support from contractors, family, friends and her professional network.In 2023, Helman left her job at Shopify to focus on Warmür full time. She said the company supported her decision. Entrepreneur’s editorial introduction listed Uncommon Goods, Amazon in the United States, Canada and Australia, Walmart online, Grommet online and Staples Canada among the brand’s retail channels. The distribution network illustrates how the company expanded beyond its own online store while remaining a small operation. It also brought new demands, including production planning, inventory management and customer service, that are more complex than selling directly through a small e-commerce site.Warmür’s design upgrade, customs challenges and path to $1 millionThe business has also had to adapt its product and operations as demand grew. For its first 4 years, Warmür used a design close to the original prototype. Helman said she collected customer feedback before developing an updated version with several practical changes. The revised design included a zipper to accommodate chairs with headrests, front buttons to help keep the blanket in place, and tassels and fringe intended to make it blend more naturally with office decor. The company also added a fleece layer to the outer knit material to make the inside feel more like a conventional blanket. Helman also described difficulties with an import from a new factory in China to Canada. She said she had expected the shipment to arrive within about 2 weeks, but it was flagged in customs. The experience involved approximately three and a half weeks of late-night and early-morning communication with the factory. She said the episode taught her to allow more time for imports and keep customers informed when delivery expectations change.Warmür also received publicity through its inclusion in gift bags for 2026 Oscar nominees. In her account for Entrepreneur, Helman said the company had sent 45 blankets to nominees and first-time directors as part of its promotional activity around the Academy Awards. Such placements can raise brand awareness, although they do not by themselves establish how much additional revenue they generate. According to Entrepreneur’s editorial introduction, Warmür spent its first few years building to $150,000 in revenue. The introduction also reported approximately $200,000 in sales across direct sales and wholesale between July and December 2025, following the product relaunch. Entrepreneur’s editorial introduction put the retail value of inventory in production or in the pipeline at approximately $500,000. That figure represents potential retail value, not revenue already earned, and does not establish how much of the inventory will ultimately sell.Entrepreneur’s headline and editorial introduction framed $1 million in sales as Warmür’s target for 2026. Published in May, that figure was a projection rather than a confirmed result. The material cited here does not establish whether the business subsequently met the target. The reported six-month sales figure of approximately $200,000 also shows that reaching the target would require substantial further growth. Helman’s story offers a practical lesson for aspiring founders: a business can begin with a small problem, but growth requires more than an original idea. Manufacturing capacity, customer feedback, reliable fulfilment and distribution all become increasingly important as demand expands. Warmür’s next milestone is to turn its growing retail presence and updated product into sustained sales that support its seven-figure ambition.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.summary: BENGALURU: A 42-year-old advocate was shot dead at his residence in Pattandur Agrahara, Whitefield, late Sunday night, allegedly by two tenants working as
articles.body: BENGALURU: A 42-year-old advocate was shot dead at his residence in Pattandur Agrahara, Whitefield, late Sunday night, allegedly by two tenants working as delivery agents following a dispute over unpaid rent.The suspects, identified as Pankaj Dube and Amit Kumar Dube, both from Bihar, had been living in a small room behind the house of B Manjunath for around one-and-a-half years. Police said the duo had not paid rent for three months.Unpaid rent leads to confrontationAccording to the police complaint lodged by Manjunath’s brother Muniraju, the advocate reprimanded the tenants over the pending rent on Sunday night. The confrontation is suspected to have led to the murder.“First, they came near the house and spoke to Manjunath for some time. Saying they would return with the money, they went back. Around 11.45pm, one of them returned and called Manjunath out,” Muniraju said.One tenant hands over cash, the other allegedly opens fireA close relative, Akshay, said one of the suspects handed over the rent to Manjunath. As the advocate counted the cash, the other suspect allegedly approached him from behind and shot him in the head.Manjunath was rushed to hospital, where doctors declared him dead despite attempts to revive him. He is survived by his wife and two minor children.Deputy commissioner of police (Whitefield) Saiduly Adavat said police launched a manhunt for the suspects, who allegedly fled on separate motorcycles.Another senior police officer said investigators had leads on the suspects’ whereabouts and were probing how they obtained the firearm.Police probe source of illegal firearmA senior officer expressed concern over the alleged use of an illegal pistol in the killing. Police will investigate where the weapon was purchased and whether the suspects’ associates or relatives possess other illegal firearms, the officer said.Manjunath’s family has four siblings, and the family’s ancestral properties include extensive landholdings and buildings, police said. Advocates’ association seeks speedy investigationCondemning the killing, Advocates’ Association Bengaluru president Subba Reddy said representatives of the organisation met police commissioner Seemanth Kumar Singh and sought a speedy investigation.The association also discussed the need for guidelines for private firms hiring workers from other states and for house owners renting accommodation to them, he said.Manjunath’s neighbour Siddegowda expressed shock over the incident and called for measures to prevent similar attacks. Killing follows shooting over business disputeThe murder comes a week after a realtor allegedly shot and injured his former car driver near Konanakunte over a business dispute. The realtor allegedly fired a round into the driver’s leg using his licensed revolver. Police arrested him and seized the weapon. articles.title: ‘Not getting involved in Israeli elections’: JD Vance on Netanyahu re-election
articles.summary: US Vice President JD Vance on Monday declined to endorse Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for re-election, a day after President Donald Trump
articles.body: US Vice President JD Vance on Monday declined to endorse Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for re-election, a day after President Donald Trump backed the embattled Israeli leader.“The president has the most influential endorsement in American or international political history,” Vance said during an interview with journalist Mark Halperin.Asked about his position, Vance said he would focus on US elections rather than get involved in Israeli politics.“I endorse American candidates, and that’s where I’m focused on the midterms,” Vance said while travelling to campaign for Republican Senate nominee Michael Whatley of North Carolina. “So, I’m not getting involved in Israeli elections.”Vance has previously campaigned for a foreign leader, travelling to Hungary last spring to support then-prime minister Viktor Orban before his party lost the parliamentary election.His refusal to follow Trump’s lead on Netanyahu comes at a sensitive time for Jewish Americans and US-Israel relations, with concerns over antisemitism rising ahead of the US midterm elections.Republicans have sought to portray Democrats, including Michigan Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed, as hostile towards Jews and Israel, even as divisions persist within their own party.Vance has also faced questions from Jewish Republicans about his commitment to Jewish Americans and the US alliance with Israel. Last month, he addressed the Republican Jewish Coalition in Las Vegas, leaving a positive impression while stopping short of distancing himself from conservative podcast host Tucker Carlson.Carlson faced criticism last year for interviewing antisemite Nick Fuentes on his podcast.Vance has also criticised elements of Netanyahu’s government over the war with Iran. In June, he sharply criticised Israeli officials who opposed Trump’s efforts to resolve the conflict. A month later, he alleged that some Israeli officials had attempted to influence American public opinion to derail negotiations.“There are some people within their system that we know beyond a shadow of a doubt are manipulating and trying to change American public opinion to keep the war going on indefinitely,” Vance said during an appearance on Joe Rogan’s podcast.You use AI every day. articles.title: Donald Trump approval hits record low of 31% as midterms near, Democrats lead by 12 points
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump’s approval rating has fallen to a record low of 31%, with rising gasoline prices and concerns over the economy weighing on
articles.body: US President Donald Trump’s approval rating has fallen to a record low of 31%, with rising gasoline prices and concerns over the economy weighing on public sentiment ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll that concluded on Monday.The four-day survey found that Trump's approval rating dropped by one percentage point from two weeks earlier, marking the lowest level of either of his presidential terms. The poll also showed Democrats opening a 12-point lead over Republicans among registered voters, the widest margin recorded during the current election cycle.Asked which party they would support if congressional elections were held today, 47% of registered voters chose Democrats, compared with 35% who backed Republicans.The Democratic lead has widened from seven percentage points in the previous Reuters/Ipsos poll conducted two weeks earlier, when Democrats had 44% support against 37% for Republicans.However, national polls do not capture all the nuances of state-level Senate races and district-level House contests, where Republicans retain some structural advantages.Women voters drive shift towards democratsThe widening Democratic lead was partly driven by a larger share of women saying they would vote for Democratic candidates. Around 50% of female voters backed Democrats, compared with 32% who said they would vote Republican.Men also favoured Democrats, although the gap between the two parties was narrower among male voters.Trump's popularity has suffered since he ordered military strikes on Iran in February alongside US ally Israel. The war triggered a surge in gasoline prices, putting additional pressure on household finances.The poll found that 68% of Americans disapproved of Trump's handling of the economy. The figure included 37% of respondents who identified themselves as Republicans.When asked which party would do a better job managing the economy, 40% of respondents chose Democrats, compared with 33% who favoured Republicans.You use AI every day. articles.title: What if the next US president turns hostile? Netanyahu's answer lies partly in India
articles.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has warned that a future US president could be hostile towards Israel, calling for new alliances with countries
articles.body: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has warned that a future US president could be hostile towards Israel, calling for new alliances with countries such as India and nations in Latin America to safeguard his country's strategic interests.Netanyahu unveiled his security doctrine on Sunday, nine days before Israel's October 27 election, arguing that Israel must prepare for a possible shift in Washington's approach. His remarks came hours before US President Donald Trump publicly endorsed his re-election bid."In two years, a President, man or woman, could come to power who is very hostile to Israel," Netanyahu said."How would you deal with that? How would you operate in relation to the United States? And beyond that, what solutions would be necessary?", he questioned.The Israeli premier stressed that his government must make the most of the remaining years of Trump's presidency while preparing for an uncertain political future in the US."First, we must do everything we can during these two years, and during the following two years, in the American arena, through good times and bad," he said.Netanyahu also called for Israel to broaden its network of international partners, pointing to India as a key ally beyond the US."The second thing is to create other alliances. That is what I am working on now with many countries in our region and outside it. India is not a small country, and there are many others," the Israeli Prime Minister emphasised.He also pointed to shifting political dynamics in Latin America as an opportunity to expand Israel's diplomatic reach."There is a major shift in Latin America, and there could be an enormous change in Brazil in just a few days," Netanyahu said, adding, "We must expand our pool of alliances and develop capabilities that make us valuable to everyone."Netanyahu has repeatedly cited his relationship with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and India's ties with Israel to counter perceptions that his country is becoming diplomatically isolated.In May this year, amid a prolonged war and growing international criticism, he described the relationship with India as "unique", calling the country a "huge power" where there is "crazy love" for Israel.Netanyahu's US dilemmaNetanyahu's warning comes amid concerns in Israel over declining support among Democrats in the US. Analysts have attributed some of the strain to his strained relations with Democratic presidents Barack Obama and Joe Biden.Those tensions have also featured in Netanyahu's political messaging. He has presented his willingness to challenge American presidents as a sign of a strong leader prepared to defend Israel's interests, a strategy analysts believe has helped him politically over the years.Netanyahu is Israel's longest-serving prime minister.Rival slams security doctrineNetanyahu's presentation drew sharp criticism from Gadi Eisenkot, his main challenger in the upcoming election. The former Israel Defence Forces chief dismissed the announcement as a political exercise that offered little substance as the country continued to face security challenges."Nine days before the election and three years after the gravest failure and disaster in Israel's history, with every war front still open, Netanyahu decided to present his 'security doctrine' to the public," Eisenkot said."Two hollow pages, full of slogans that have nothing whatsoever to do with a security doctrine, reveal more than anything the strategic vacuum Netanyahu has left the State of Israel in and his disregard for the security of Israeli citizens," he said.Eisenkot accused Netanyahu of using fear and political messaging to influence voters ahead of the election."This is Netanyahu's method: manipulating perceptions, frightening people and trying to divert attention from the parade of lies and racism surrounding his campaign tonight," he said.You use AI every day. articles.title: A forgotten red chalk drawing of a crouching child surfaced in an Italian collection; experts believe it could be an undiscovered work by Édouard Manet
articles.summary: A small red chalk drawing of a crouching child has emerged from a private collection in northern Italy, and specialists believe it came from the hand of
articles.body: A small red chalk drawing of a crouching child has emerged from a private collection in northern Italy, and specialists believe it came from the hand of Édouard Manet, the nineteenth-century French painter who helped launch modern art. The sheet had sat quietly in obscurity, with no scholar studying it, until a visiting art historian noticed it and recognised something special. The attribution rests on a faded studio stamp, a distinctive drawing style, and a striking resemblance to figures in some of Manet's most celebrated canvases. This is how the discovery unfolded, why experts are excited, and what remains unanswered.How an art historian spotted an unstudied red chalk drawing in a private collection in northern ItalyThe discovery began when Francesco Baccanelli, an art historian who specialises in seventeenth- and eighteenth-century paintings and prints from Lombardy and Veneto, visited a modest and little-known private collection in northern Italy, according to The Guardian. The owner showed him an inscription on the back of the mount naming Manet as the artist, yet no art historian had ever examined the sheet. Baccanelli told The Guardian that he was captivated at once and grew more convinced of the attribution the longer he studied it. He then sent photographs to Emily Beeny, chief curator of the Legion of Honour at the Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco, whom he regards as one of the world's leading Manet experts. Artforum's news desk likewise reported that the drawing had never been studied.Why experts believe the child is by Manet, the studio stamp, ultraviolet analysis and signature styleSeveral strands of evidence support the attribution. Ultraviolet analysis revealed Manet's faded studio stamp in the lower right-hand corner, a detail Artforum also highlights as key proof. Style points the same way. Beeny told the Guardian that the drawing shows abrupt shifts between light and shadow and peculiar plump, tapered fingers, which she called little habits typical of the painter. Artforum adds that the sheet sits comfortably beside the scores of red chalk preparatory sketches Manet produced in the mid-nineteenth century. Beeny said she felt an immediate sense of recognition on first seeing a photograph, something she had not experienced with the many supposed Manet works people send her. The small sheet measures 20.5 centimetres by 17.5 centimetres.How the crouching child connects to Manet's masterpiece ‘The Old Musician’ and ‘Le Déjeuner sur l'herbe’The child resembles a street urchin in The Old Musician, the painting in which Manet sought to show the humanity of homeless and marginalised people. Beeny said it is possible the same sitter posed for the little girl with a very similar hairstyle standing on the left in the finished canvas. Artforum, by contrast, links the figure to a street urchin in Le Déjeuner sur l'herbe from 1863, and the Guardian notes that Manet's red chalk studies relate to that painting too. The sitter's identity remains unknown. Beeny and Baccanelli mention Alexandre, a youth hired in the late 1850s to clean Manet's brushes and palettes who occasionally posed, but they note the figure appears to be a girl of perhaps six.Provenance and publication, the Burlington Magazine article and hopes for the Manet catalogue raisonnéThe drawing was sold twice in the 1930s, first in Germany and then in Switzerland, yet it never appeared in scholarly publications on the artist. Beeny and Baccanelli will publish their findings in the October issue of the Burlington Magazine, where they concede that the drawing's original purpose and early history remain unclear. Although the sheet is squared for transfer to a canvas, no such composition by Manet is known. Beeny told the Guardian that this suggests he took time and effort over it and was pleased with the result. She hopes it will be included in the next edition of the definitive Manet catalogue raisonné, produced by the Wildenstein Plattner Institute, which has not yet studied the drawing.Why a rediscovered Manet study matters for art lovers, collectors and scholars of French modernismFor admirers of French modernism, the find offers a rare window into Manet's working methods. The drawing is typical of the red chalk life studies he made in the 1850s and 1860s, shaped by his close study of Renaissance draughtsmanship in Florence, and similar sketches relate to Le Déjeuner sur l'herbe as well as The Old Musician. Beeny, whose exhibitions include Manet and Modern Beauty, staged by the Getty Museum in Los Angeles and the Art Institute of Chicago, told the Guardian she is unsure when an unpublished Manet drawing last surfaced, but it has certainly been many years. Until the Wildenstein Plattner Institute studies the sheet, the attribution remains a scholarly proposal rather than a settled verdict.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Newcastle mother's search for son fighting for Russia in Ukraine
articles.summary: Nathan Stobbart’s family say he faced deportation from Russia if he did not join the country's army.
articles.body:
British man Nathan Stobbart has been declared missing in action while fighting for Russia in Ukraine. He kept his military service a secret from his family in the UK, who are now desperately trying to find him.

In December 2025, Nathan's mother Valerie Stobbart received a text message that plunged her life into turmoil.

It was from her panic-stricken daughter-in-law, Ksenia, who lives in Russia with Valerie's 30-year-old son and the couple's newborn baby. Nathan had been fighting for the country against Ukraine and had vanished.

"I can't even describe it," Valerie says.

"I had to drive home from my daughter's house. I don't even know how I managed to drive home, quite honestly.

"I remember walking in and telling Sean [Valerie's partner], and we were just both in total shock."

Her son had told her he was working as an electrical contractor and she had no idea he had joined the Russian army in April last year.

"You think that somebody is living this lovely little life with a new family and then suddenly you find out that they've gone, they're missing," she says.

"They've completely disappeared off the face of the earth."

Nathan's voice was last heard on his military radio a week before Ksenia's message.

A Russian army document, seen by the BBC, shows he was officially declared missing in action by his unit on 12 December but no body has been found.

Valerie says Ksenia revealed the Russian authorities had warned Nathan he would not be granted a visa to remain in the country and faced deportation if he did not sign up for a year's military service.

Russian media has previously reported foreign men in the country have been forced to join the invasion in Ukraine in return for citizenship.

Valerie does not agree with her son's decision to fight but accepts he faced a difficult choice - he could either return home to Newcastle in north-east England without his wife and newborn son or join the Russian army.

"He was so desperate to stay with his family he would do anything," she says.

It is illegal for Britons to fight for foreign nations involved in conflicts with countries with which the UK is at peace, unless they hold dual nationality, according to the Foreign Enlistment Act 1870.

But Nathan is not the only British national without dual nationality to fight for Russian president Vladimir Putin against Ukraine.

Ben Stimson and Aiden Minnis are believed to be the first and were given Russian citizenship for fighting in the occupied Donbas region. Bradley Townsend was killed in Ukraine in June and is believed to be the first British citizen fighting for Russia to die in the conflict.

Their situation is different, Valerie says, as Nathan did not travel to Russia with the intention of fighting in the war.

"He never wanted to join the army," she says. "He was there to live with his family."

She understands people may have strong opinions about Nathan fighting for Russia and stresses she condemns the country's "awful" invasion in Ukraine.

"I really don't care about changing people's opinions," she says. "What I care about is trying to find him."

Nathan moved to Russia on Christmas Day 2024 to start a new life with Ksenia.

They had met online and she had visited him and his family in the UK.

The couple got married in Russia and were bringing up their son like a "normal, little family".

They were also raising Ksenia's three children from a previous relationship, which meant relocating the whole family to the UK was deemed unaffordable, Valerie says.

She questioned Nathan's initial decision to move to Russia but warmed to the idea because the couple lived "miles from any fighting".

They did talk about the conflict "but it was happening in Ukraine, it wasn't happening in Russia", she says.

Prior to Ksenia's text message, Valerie had no reason to believe something was not right. Receiving photos and videos of her newborn grandchild made everything feel "normal".

As the days and weeks passed since Nathan went missing, the enormity of the situation became increasingly clear.

The family discovered he had recorded a goodbye video at the start of his military service, which he sent to his wife to be passed on to his mother in the event of his death.

"I could only watch it once," Valerie says. "I had to turn it off."

Despite the video and his prolonged silence, she believes her son is still alive.

The fight for answers has been long and torturous for Valerie, who has approached the government and several charities, both in the UK and Russia.

"I contacted the Foreign Office and got a caseworker there, but they admitted themselves that they can't do anything," she says.

The Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) said it was aware of reports a British national was missing after fighting for Russia in Ukraine and was "in contact with his family".

It said it advised against all travel to Russia and "our ability to provide consular support in these circumstances is severely limited".

Questions to Russia about Nathan's last known whereabouts failed to provide any leads. "They just kept saying everything was classified," Valerie says. "They wouldn't even tell us where he was."

All of Valerie's spare time is spent trawling the internet for clues.

"The days just roll on, the weeks roll on," she says, wiping away tears. "We're nine months down the line with no more answers than we had in the beginning."

But she still has hope he may be captured, but alive. and watches official body exchanges between Russia and Ukraine on the news service Reuters. No reports have contained Nathan's name.

She remains hopeful he would at least be identified, because the Russian authorities have his DNA from his baby.

Valerie's investigations led her to a report in The Telegraph newspaper about a Ukrainian prisoner-of-war camp but the journalist who wrote it could not remember seeing Nathan during his visit.

Although she did not agree to be interviewed, that contact was to have consequences.

She told her employer at the Home Office, where she worked as an asylum decision maker, that Nathan had disappeared in Russia and she had sought help from the reporter.

She says she was immediately sent home from work and suspended, pending a disciplinary hearing, at which she was sacked for gross misconduct because contacting the media was in breach of her contract.

She explained she had spoken to the journalist "purely to find information" and did not disclose where she worked but lost an appeal against the decision.

The Home Office told the BBC it did not comment on individual employment cases.

With "nothing to lose", Valerie contacted the journalist to share her story of Nathan's disappearance and of losing her job.

She hoped the article would be seen by someone who had been in contact with her son, but it attracted little sympathy from people online who were critical of his decision to fight for Russia.

"I did read some of the comments when the article went out but I stopped because they were just awful," she says.

Now, she lives in "limbo every day", not willing to give up the search for her son, clinging to the hope he will be found alive, but having exhausted all avenues for help.

"Every single day I think my phone could go and somebody somewhere is going to say 'we've found him'," she says.

"I have read reports of Russians that have turned up after a year of being in captivity, or whatever, and their families thought they were dead.

"So every day there is a new hope he could be found."

articles.title: Locals and carnival icons in Notting Hill Frieze exhibition
articles.summary: London street artist Endless's new installation, Endless Frieze, includes buildings and street scenes.
articles.body:
A fourth-generation Portobello market trader, a Notting Hill Carnival stalwart and fashion icon known locally as "Notting Hill's best dressed man" are among the people featured in a new artwork by street artist Endless, about Notting Hill's identity.

The installation, Endless Frieze, displays local buildings and street scenes celebrating the west London neighbourhood as part of the annual art fair Frieze London.

Guests and celebrities specifically chosen for their contribution to the area's identity were photographed during a live event on Friday and now feature as part of the exhibition.

The work is "about the community and bringing them into the art world and into my world," Endless said.

This world includes Cheryl Devlin, a greengrocer whose family have had a fruit and vegetable stall in the market for more than a hundred years. She has worked on the stall since she was five years old.

"I used to stand beside my mum and dad and sell lemons, five for a shilling," she says.

"And if you didn't, you didn't get your dinner; it was really that tough in the '50s."

The area has changed since then, she says. There used to be around 350 people selling fruit and veg, but that's been replaced with stalls selling cooked food or bric-a-brac.

"A lot of people downsize who can't afford the housing.

"It's just tough to live around this area now where it was quite cheap and reasonable."

Like the area, the exhibition is ever-changing. It's being created in real time - as soon as the portraits are taken they appear on the wall, in a collage - something Endless says can be a creative risk.

"It becomes a frieze, a moment in time of the architecture, the buildings and the people. So it's really about the energy of the place.

"Whenever I make any artwork, I plan it and I have a vision, but then it can go either way," he says.

"There's like elements of risk even when you're making a painting. So with this the risk is life, anything could happen. So the camera could go wrong or I could stick it up wrong but that's part of it.

"In art we say it's like a happy accident and that's when something good happens as well."

Also part of the artwork, and perhaps a gift to photograph is Jama Elmi, a recognisable individual who admits he is a "local icon".

"Notting Hill, it's vibrant, the energy, the love, it's absolutely, I wouldn't live anywhere else but here," he says.

For Allyson Williams MBE, Notting Hill simply is the carnival. She is a board member of Notting Hill Carnival Limited and has been involved with its organisation since 1975.

In 1980, she launched her own costume brand with her husband, called Genesis Mask Band.

"I have been a seamstress, I've been a designer. I've been bringing the costumes - the designs of my husband and my daughter - bringing the costumes to life."

Part of the reason she loves the carnival is because it is part of her history.

"I'm a Trinidadian and so it all started there and it was the Trinidadians who came, who were part of the Windrush generation who came and brought all the art and culture here," she says.

Karl Amata works at Sound Records on All Saints Road. He says the exhibition is a good thing.

"I hope it continues. We need more things like this to bring the community together.

"Because there's the lack of it. Everything's been shut down, the shops, every cultural centre, anywhere people can gather together."

Karen Millen, founder of the Karen Millen clothing brand said she was "very honoured" to be part of the installation.

She added Notting Hill is the "epicentre of where people come for creation really, so I don't think that will ever go away."

The exhibition at the Cris Contini Contemporary Gallery runs till the end of October.
